title: Loop Control Statements: break and continue
learningObjectives: Distinguish break from continue in loop execution.
Explain how break exits the nearest enclosing loop immediately.
Explain how continue skips the remainder of the current iteration.
Trace continue in for loops, including the update step that still runs.
Use loop-control statements carefully to keep loops readable and terminating.

understand.concept: Loop-control statements change normal flow inside a loop. break ends the nearest enclosing loop immediately and execution continues after that loop. continue skips the remaining statements in the current iteration and moves to the next iteration. These affect only the nearest loop that contains the statement; in nested loops, the outer loop continues after the inner loop ends.
understand.whyItMatters: They can avoid unnecessary work or skip items that should not be processed, but confusing them can cause missing output, unexpected termination, or incorrect loop updates.
understand.analogy: At a checkpoint, break means leave the whole queue-processing activity; continue means skip the current person and check the next one.
understand.analogyLimit: Real programs may have multiple nested loops and other control-flow paths, so trace which loop contains each statement instead of relying on the analogy.

explain.narrative: A break statement exits the closest loop immediately. A continue statement ends the current iteration early. In a for loop, continue still proceeds to the loop's update expression and then checks the condition. In a while loop, continue returns to the condition; if the loop counter is updated inside the body, ensure that update is not accidentally skipped or the loop may never progress. In nested loops, break or continue affects the nearest loop, not every loop.

examples.title: break exits at the first matching value
examples.explanation: When n reaches 4, break ends this loop; 4, 5, and 6 are not processed.

examples.title: continue skips one iteration
examples.explanation: At n=3, continue skips the output, then the for-loop update advances n to 4.

examples.title: Skip non-positive values
examples.explanation: continue skips values that are zero or negative; only positive values reach output.

examples.title: break affects only the inner loop
examples.explanation: Each inner loop ends at col 3, but the outer loop continues with the next row.

examples.title: continue in a for loop still runs its update
examples.explanation: Even values are skipped; n++ still executes after continue so the loop progresses.

commonMistakes: Treating break and continue as interchangeable.
Assuming break exits every nested loop instead of only the nearest loop.
Expecting statements after continue in the same iteration to run.
Forgetting that a for-loop update still runs after continue.
Using continue in a while loop before an essential counter update, causing an infinite loop.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Skip a value and stop at a limit
guidedTask.instructions: Print numbers 1 through 8, skip 5, and stop when the loop reaches 7.
steps: Start a for loop with n from 1 through 8.
If n equals 5, use continue to skip printing it.
If n equals 7, use break before printing it.
Trace the output to confirm skipped and stopping values.

independentTask.title: Independent: Filter and stop in a scan
independentTask.instructions: Given [-3, 12, 8, 0, 19, 6, -2], print positive values but stop when you encounter 19.
requirements: Use a for...of loop to visit values in order.
Use continue to skip values that are not positive.
Use break when the value is 19, before printing it.
Print each positive value encountered before 19.

hints: break ends the closest loop, not automatically every nested loop.
Place break before output when the stopping value should not print.
continue skips statements after it in the current iteration.
In a for loop, continue still runs the update expression.
In a while loop, ensure a counter update is not skipped by continue.
Trace nested loops by identifying which loop contains the control statement.

questions.prompt: What does break do inside a loop?
options: Ends the nearest enclosing loop immediately
questions.answer: Ends the nearest enclosing loop immediately
questions.explanation: break exits the closest loop and execution continues after it.

options: Skips the remainder of the current iteration
questions.answer: Skips the remainder of the current iteration
questions.explanation: continue abandons the current iteration and moves toward the next one.

questions.prompt: In a for loop, what happens after continue?
options: The update expression is skipped permanently
The update expression runs, then the condition is checked
questions.answer: The update expression runs, then the condition is checked
questions.explanation: A for-loop continue moves to the update step before the next condition test.

questions.prompt: In a nested loop, which loop does break exit?
questions.explanation: A break in the inner loop ends that loop; the outer loop may continue.

questions.prompt: Why can continue cause a while loop to run forever?
options: It changes the condition to true
It may skip an essential body-side counter update
questions.answer: It may skip an essential body-side counter update
questions.explanation: If progress depends on an update inside the body and continue skips it, the condition may stay true indefinitely.
